subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Management Approach & Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM)
question: Under Ind AS 108, how is an 'Operating Segment' identified, and who constitutes the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM)?
options: Identified based on statutory tax reporting circles; CODM is always the statutory auditor.

Identified using the 'Management Approach' based on internal organizational units whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the CODM (a function, not necessarily a title, which allocates resources and assesses performance of segments).
Identified strictly by physical geographic pin codes.
Identified based on products with identical gross profit margins.
ref: Ind AS 108 (Operating Segments) - Paragraphs 5-7: Definition of Operating Segment & CODM
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 5 defines an operating segment as a component of an entity: (a) that engages in business activities from which it may earn revenues and incur expenses; (b) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the entity's Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) to make decisions about resources and assess performance; and (c) for which discrete financial information is available. The CODM is a function that allocates resources.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Quantitative Thresholds (10% Tests)
question: A conglomerate has 6 internal operating divisions. Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 13, which of the following quantitative thresholds mandates that an operating segment must be reported separately?
options: Its reported revenue (including both internal and external sales) is 10% or more of the combined revenue of all operating segments.

The absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10% or more of the greater, in absolute amount, of: (i) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss; and (ii) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that reported a loss.
Its assets are 10% or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.
Meeting ANY ONE of the three 10% criteria (Revenue, Profit/Loss, or Assets) makes the segment reportable.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 13: The 10% Quantitative Thresholds
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 13 specifies that an entity shall report separately information about an operating segment that meets any of the following quantitative thresholds: (a) revenue (internal + external) >= 10% of combined revenue; (b) profit/loss >= 10% of the greater of combined profitable segments and combined loss segments; or (c) assets >= 10% of combined assets.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: The 75% External Revenue Sufficiency Rule
question: After applying the 10% quantitative thresholds, a conglomerate's reportable segments account for only 60% of total consolidated external revenue. What action is required under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 15?
options: No action; remaining 40% is omitted.

Additional operating segments must be identified as reportable segments (even if they do not meet the 10% thresholds) until at least 75% of the entity's total external revenue is included in reportable segments.
The entity must prepare financial statements on a single-segment basis.
The threshold is relaxed to 50% for Indian entities.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 15: The 75% External Revenue Threshold
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 15 explicitly mandates: 'If the total external revenue reported by operating segments constitutes less than 75% of the entity's revenue, additional operating segments shall be identified as reportable segments (even if they do not meet the criteria in paragraph 13) until at least 75% of the entity's revenue is included in reportable segments.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Major Customer Disclosure Threshold
question: Under Ind AS 108, when is an entity required to disclose information about its reliance on major customers?
options: When any single customer accounts for more than 1% of total revenues.

If revenues from transactions with a single external customer amount to 10% or more of an entity's total revenues, the entity shall disclose that fact, the total amount of revenues from each such customer, and the identity of the segment(s) reporting the revenues (the name of the customer need not be disclosed).
Only when the customer is a government ministry.
Major customer disclosures are prohibited for confidentiality.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 34: Information About Major Customers
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 34 states: 'If revenues from transactions with a single external customer amount to 10 per cent or more of an entity's revenues, the entity shall disclose that fact, the total amount of revenues from each such customer, and the identity of the segment or segments reporting the revenues. The entity need not disclose the identity of a major customer or the amount of revenues that each segment reports from that customer.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Effective Annual Tax Rate in Interim Reporting
question: Under Ind AS 34, how should interim income tax expense be measured and recognized?
options: Calculated by applying statutory tax slabs to the actual profit of each individual interim quarter without regard to annual forecasts.
Measured using the best estimate of the weighted average annual effective income tax rate expected for the full financial year applied to the pre-tax income of the interim period.
Income tax is recognized only in the fourth quarter when the final tax return is filed.
Measured as a flat 25% of interim EBITDA.
ref: Ind AS 34 (Interim Financial Reporting) - Paragraphs 30(c) & Appendix B Paragraph B12
explanation: Ind AS 34 states that interim period income tax expense is accrued using the tax rate that would be applicable to expected total annual earnings, that is, the estimated average annual effective income tax rate applied to the pre-tax income of the interim period. This reflects the principle that taxes are assessed on an annual basis.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Uneven and Seasonal Revenues in Interim Periods
question: A ski resort and winter clothing manufacturer earns 85% of its annual sales revenues in Quarter 3 (October to December). How should revenue be recognized in interim financial statements under Ind AS 34?
options: Anticipated annual revenues must be averaged and smoothed equally across all 4 quarters.

Revenues that are received seasonally, cyclically, or occasionally within a financial year shall NOT be anticipated or deferred for interim reporting purposes unless anticipation or deferral would also be appropriate at the end of the financial year (revenues are recognized when earned in Quarter 3).
Quarter 1 and 2 revenues must be boosted by a management estimate.
Interim reporting is prohibited for seasonal businesses.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Paragraph 37: Revenues Received Seasonally, Cyclically, or Occasionally
explanation: Ind AS 34 Paragraph 37 explicitly specifies: 'Revenues that are received seasonally, cyclically, or occasionally within a financial year shall not be anticipated or deferred for interim reporting purposes if anticipation or deferral would not be appropriate at the end of the entity's financial year.' Seasonal revenues are recognized when they occur.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Uneven Costs Incurred in Interim Periods
question: In Quarter 1, an enterprise incurs its entire annual advertising campaign expenditure of ₹12 Crores. Management proposes deferring ₹9 Crores to Quarters 2, 3, and 4 on the grounds that advertising benefits sales throughout the year. Is this permitted under Ind AS 34?
options: Yes, advertising must be matched with future quarterly sales.

No, costs that are incurred unevenly during an entity's financial year shall be anticipated or deferred for interim reporting purposes if, and only if, it is also appropriate to anticipate or defer that type of cost at the end of the financial year; advertising costs cannot be deferred under Ind AS 38 and must be expensed in Quarter 1.
Permitted only if approved by SEBI.
Advertising is recognized in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Paragraph 39: Costs Incurred Unevenly During the Financial Year
explanation: Ind AS 34 Paragraph 39 states that an entity applies the same recognition criteria in its interim financial statements as in its annual financial statements. Because advertising costs cannot be capitalized as assets under Ind AS 38 at year-end, they cannot be deferred at an interim reporting date.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Aggregation Criteria for Operating Segments
question: Two operating segments produce consumer goods. Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 12, when may two or more operating segments be aggregated into a single reportable operating segment?
options: Whenever their combined revenues exceed ₹1,000 Crores.

Only if aggregation is consistent with the core principle of Ind AS 108, the segments have similar economic characteristics (e.g. similar long-term average gross margins), and they are similar in all of: (a) nature of products/services; (b) nature of production processes; (c) type of customer; (d) distribution methods; and (e) regulatory environment.
Whenever the CODM decides to streamline presentation.
Aggregation is never permitted under Ind AS 108.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 12: Aggregation Criteria
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 12 permits two or more operating segments to be aggregated into a single operating segment if aggregation is consistent with the core principle of the standard, the segments have similar economic characteristics, and the segments are similar in each of the five specified respects (products, production, customers, distribution, and regulatory environment).

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Year-to-Date vs Quarter Comparatives
question: For an entity whose financial year ends on 31st March, what comparative periods are required for the Statement of Profit and Loss in its interim financial report for the second quarter (30th September 2023) under Ind AS 34?
options: Only the current quarter (Q2) and previous quarter (Q1).

Statement of profit and loss for the current interim period (3 months ending 30th Sept 2023) and cumulatively for the current financial year to date (6 months ending 30th Sept 2023), with comparative statements of profit and loss for the comparable interim periods (3 months and 6 months ending 30th Sept 2022).
Only the preceding full financial year.
Comparison with the projected annual budget.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Paragraph 20(b): Comparative Periods for Statement of Profit and Loss
explanation: Under Ind AS 34 Paragraph 20(b), an interim financial report shall include statements of profit and loss for: the current interim period and cumulatively for the current financial year to date, with comparative statements of profit and loss for the comparable interim periods (current and year-to-date) of the immediately preceding financial year.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Measurement of Segment Assets and Liabilities
question: Under Ind AS 108, what accounting policies and measurement bases govern the reported amounts of segment profit or loss, segment assets, and segment liabilities?
options: They must strictly conform to Ind AS measurement rules applied in consolidated financial statements.

The amount of each segment item reported shall be the measure reported to the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) for the purposes of allocating resources to the segment and assessing its performance, accompanied by reconciliations to consolidated totals.
They must be measured at historical cost.
They are measured under tax accounting rules.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraphs 25-28: Measurement of Segment Information
explanation: Ind AS 108 follows a strict management approach: the amount of each segment item reported is the measure reported to the CODM. If the CODM uses non-Ind AS measures (e.g. operating EBITDA or management transfer pricing) to evaluate performance, those exact figures are reported in the segment note, with a formal reconciliation to consolidated financial statements under Paragraph 28.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Impairment Loss Recognized in an Interim Period
question: In Quarter 1 of FY 2023-24, an entity recognized an impairment loss of ₹10 Crores on Goodwill under Ind AS 36. By Quarter 4, economic recovery occurred, and the recoverable amount surpassed original book value. Can the goodwill impairment loss recognized in Quarter 1 be reversed in Quarter 4 of the same financial year under Ind AS 34 / Appendix A?
options: Yes, because interim reports are merely working drafts of the full annual report.
No, Appendix A of Ind AS 34 (IFRIC 10) explicitly states that an entity shall not reverse an impairment loss recognized in a previous interim period in respect of goodwill.
Reversal is permitted up to 50%.
Reversal is credited to OCI.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Appendix A (Interim Financial Reporting and Impairment) - Paragraphs 8-9
explanation: Appendix A to Ind AS 34 addresses the interaction between Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 36 regarding goodwill. It states unequivocally: 'An entity shall not reverse an impairment loss recognized in a previous interim period in respect of goodwill.' The frequency of reporting does not affect the measurement at year-end.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Geographical Disclosures
question: An Indian multinational entity operates globally. Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 32, what entity-wide geographical information must be disclosed, regardless of segment organization?
options: List of every country where products are sold.

(a) Revenues from external customers: (i) attributed to the entity's country of domicile; and (ii) attributed to all foreign countries in total; and (b) Non-current assets (other than financial instruments, deferred tax assets, and post-employment benefit assets) located in domicile vs foreign countries.
Exchange rates used in all export invoices.
Passports of international directors.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 32: Geographical Information Disclosures
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 32 mandates entity-wide geographical disclosures: external revenues attributed to the country of domicile vs foreign countries in total (with separate disclosure of any individual material foreign country); and non-current assets located in domicile vs foreign countries.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Employer Year-End Bonuses
question: An entity pays an annual incentive bonus to managers based on achieving annual turnover targets. In Quarter 2, half-yearly performance demonstrates that achieving the annual turnover target is probable, and management has a constructive obligation. How should the bonus be accounted for in the Quarter 2 interim report?
options: Recognize zero bonus until the annual target is officially audited at year-end.

A bonus is anticipated for interim reporting purposes if, and only if: (a) the bonus is a legal or constructive obligation and a reliable estimate can be made; and (b) achieving target is probable; the estimated annual bonus is accrued pro-rata over the quarters.
Charge 100% of the annual bonus in Quarter 2.
Recognize bonus in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Appendix B Paragraph B6: Year-End Bonuses
explanation: Under Appendix B of Ind AS 34, a bonus is anticipated for interim reporting purposes if, and only if, the bonus is a legal obligation or past practice makes the bonus a constructive obligation for which the entity has no realistic alternative but to make the payments, and a reliable estimate of the obligation can be made.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Discontinued Operations in Segment Reporting
question: If an operating segment meets the criteria to be classified as a Discontinued Operation under Ind AS 105, how is it presented in the segment note under Ind AS 108?
options: It must be completely removed from all segment disclosures.

It continues to be reported in segment disclosures if its information is regularly reviewed by the CODM, but must be reconciled to the continuing operations presented on the face of the financial statements.
It is presented in a separate column labeled 'Liquidated'.
All segment reporting is suspended.
ref: Ind AS 108 & Ind AS 105: Discontinued Operations in Segment Disclosures
explanation: Segment reporting reflects how the CODM views the business. If the CODM continues to monitor the discontinued segment until final disposal, it is reported in segment disclosures, accompanied by appropriate reconciliations reconciling segment totals to continuing operations.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Inventory Market Declines and Recoveries
question: In Quarter 2, commodity inventory was written down by ₹5 Crores to net realizable value under Ind AS 2. In Quarter 4, spot market prices surged. Can the ₹5 Crores inventory write-down be reversed in Quarter 4?
options: No, interim write-downs can never be reversed.

Yes, unlike goodwill, inventory write-downs are required to be reversed under Ind AS 2 when circumstances change, and this applies equally between interim periods of the same financial year (up to original cost).
Reversed only up to 50%.
Reversed into OCI.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Appendix B Paragraph B17 & Ind AS 2
explanation: Ind AS 34 Appendix B Paragraph B17 states that inventory is measured for interim reporting by the same principles as at year-end. If an inventory write-down to net realizable value is recognized in an interim period and that NRV subsequently increases in a later interim period, the write-down is reversed in accordance with Ind AS 2.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Practical Limit on Number of Reportable Segments
question: Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 19, what is the practical upper limit on the number of reportable segments beyond which segment information may become overly detailed and lose usefulness?
options: 5 segments.

Approximately 10 reportable segments; when the number of reportable segments increases above 10, the entity should consider whether a practical limit has been reached and whether segments should be aggregated.
25 segments.
No limit exists.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 19: Practical Limit of Ten Segments
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 19 states: 'There may be a practical limit to the number of reportable segments that an entity discloses... When the number of reportable segments increases above ten, the entity should consider whether a practical limit has been reached.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Materiality in Interim Reports
question: Under Ind AS 34, how is materiality assessed when deciding how to recognize, measure, classify, or disclose an item for interim financial reporting?
options: Assessed exclusively in relation to projected annual financial data.

Assessed in relation to the interim period financial data itself; while interim measurements may rely more on estimates than annual data, materiality is evaluated in the context of the interim period to ensure interim statements are not misleading.
Materiality is fixed at 1% of equity.
Materiality rules do not apply to interim reports.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Paragraphs 23-25: Materiality in Interim Reporting
explanation: Ind AS 34 Paragraph 23 states: 'In deciding how to recognize, measure, classify, or disclose an item for interim financial reporting purposes, materiality shall be assessed in relation to the interim period financial data.' It recognizes that interim measurements may involve greater use of estimates than annual reports.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Restatement of Previously Reported Segments
question: In FY 2023-24, an entity reorganizes its internal management structure, altering the composition of its reportable segments. Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 29, how should comparative segment information for prior periods be presented?
options: Comparative information is not required for segment changes.
The entity shall restate the comparative information for earlier periods (including interim periods) unless the information is not available and the cost to develop it would be excessive.
Comparative information must use statutory tax circles.
Prior years must be re-audited by NFRA.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 29: Restatement of Previously Reported Segment Information
explanation: Ind AS 108 Paragraph 29 states that if an entity changes the structure of its internal organization in a manner that causes the composition of its reportable segments to change, the corresponding information for earlier periods shall be restated unless the information is not available and the cost to develop it would be excessive.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 34: Component Accounting and Interim Depreciation
question: During Quarter 1, an enterprise acquires an item of plant. In calculating depreciation for the Quarter 1 interim report, should depreciation be calculated on a full-year basis or based on the fraction of the year the asset was operational?
options: Full annual depreciation must be recognized in Quarter 1.
Depreciation is recognized based on the period during which the asset was available for use during the interim period (apportioned for the 3 months or relevant active fraction).
No depreciation is recognized in interim quarters.
Depreciation is recognized only in Quarter 4.
ref: Ind AS 34 - Principles of Interim Recognition
explanation: Depreciation in an interim period reflects the consumption of economic benefits during that specific interim timeframe. Assets acquired during the interim period are depreciated from the date they are available for use over the fraction of the interim period.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 108: Symmetrical Allocation of Assets and Expenses
question: Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 27, if a segment expense (such as depreciation) is included in the measure of segment profit or loss reported to the CODM, must the related asset also be included in segment assets?
options: No, assets and expenses can be completely mismatched.

Yes, segment assets shall include those assets used by a segment and either allocated to, or used by, that segment in its operations; if depreciation is allocated to a segment, the related asset is symmetrically included in segment assets unless management reports them asymmetrically to the CODM.
Assets are never reported in operating segments.
Only cash can be allocated.
ref: Ind AS 108 - Paragraph 27: Symmetrical Allocation
explanation: Under Ind AS 108 Paragraph 27, the allocation of assets and liabilities to segments must be consistent with the allocation of related income and expenses (symmetrical allocation). If an item of depreciation is included in segment profit or loss, the underlying asset is typically included in segment assets.
